Heraklion Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Iraklio, Greece

Demolished. Jewish presence in Heraklion is documented from the 12th century, flourishing under Venetian rule from 1204; by the 14th century, Jews lived in a ghetto with four synagogues, and the community became known for its efforts to ransom captives. An 1845 earthquake destroyed most Jewish homes and both existing synagogues, and an 1884 blood libel accusation followed — one of several such cases recorded in this collection, alongside Hungary and Poland. By 1897 only 20 families remained, and a German aerial attack in May 1941 destroyed the community's sole remaining synagogue; only three Jews survived the war in hiding. The cemetery, presumed to date to around the 13th century, has been completely demolished — a stadium and residential buildings now occupy the site, alongside a small operating Armenian cemetery nearby.
